title: Lab Lighthouse: weekly research notes — quant/evals/onboarding
summary: Weekly capture from the Lighthouse sprint: short wins on asymmetric INT4 probes, unexpected failure mode in KV prefetch with long-context, and initial onboarding notes for opt-7b variant. Plan: stabilize activation clipping, add focused eval harness for instruction-following, and schedule canary on dedicated pool next week.
content:
Attendees: Aisha, Samuel, Claire, Miguel, Rina (30m standup).

Brief highlights:
- Asymmetric INT4 probe (experiment 'a4-lighthouse') ran across 2 checkpoints of opt-7b-fp16->int4. Observed 1.8x speed vs FP16 in throughput on A10040GB microbatches but a median instr-follow pass-rate drop of 4.6% on the alignment suite.
- Discovered that activation outliers in attention layers (layers 8-10) blow up dynamic range for per-channel minmax; switched to per-channel 2-pass clip estimation which cut worst-case divergence by ~2.1x.
- KV-prefetch regression: enabling aggressive kv-prefetch for long sequences (>=2048) caused intermittent OOMs when combined with microbatching factor 4 on dedicated nodes. Root cause: host-side pre-alloc + mismatched stream sync. Repro steps added to linked notebook.
- Eval harness: added instruction-following subset (IF-80), code-execution coherence tests (CE-20), and a short hallucination probe. We now compute pass/fail + BLEU-ish for code cells for clearer signal.

Notes to self / informal:
- a4-lighthouse results are noisy; need 3x reruns with fixed seed, same warmup tokens. Current run used mixed warmup (randomized) which may bias KV cache hits.
- Claire: remind infra to pin CUDA 12.3 for the microbatch kernel benchmark. Differences seen between 12.2 and 12.3 are non-trivial.

Experiment details (quick tech):
- Name: a4-lighthouse-int4-perc
- Model: opt-7b-reshard-v2 (original FP16 checkpoint), quant path uses per-channel asymmetric 4-bit, 16-level LUT for scales, fallback path for outlier blocks to int8.
- Batch configs tried: microbatch 1/2/4 on A10040GB; continuous batching turned off for debugging.
- Observed latency P50: 78ms -> 45ms (FP16->INT4), P95: 210ms -> 190ms (INT4 slightly worse at tail, investigate scheduling).
- Token-level perplexity delta vs FP16: +0.9% on WF-100, but instruction-following delta worse on IF-80.

Blocking items:
- Need deterministic quant tool run (current tools mutate RNG of scale selection). Ticket opened (jira:AP-1782).
- KV-prefetch sync bug: requires SRE/infra spin to reproduce safely on a dedicated node (can't replicate on dev-small).
- Eval pass threshold undefined for this bootstrap; propose we use: IF-80 pass-rate >= 90% and hallucination score <= 0.12 for canary pass.

Actionable next steps (see action_items below) and tentative owners.

Design ideas / investigation threads:
- Try hybrid per-channel static + per-block dynamic clipping: maintain cheap 8-bit moving-window stats and only re-estimate full float clip for blocks showing drift. Could dramatically reduce quant noise for conversational workloads.
- Explore asymmetric zero-point tuning per attention head; early sims show some heads prefer non-zero offset reducing mse by ~6%.
- For KV-prefetch: add scoped allocator that unrolls host preallocs across microbatches instead of per-request; small patch in PR for review.

Meeting adjourn: 09:28. Quick retro: keep weekday standup to 20m, use deep-dive on Fridays for heavy experiment triage.

Unresolved questions (write-up for product/ops):
- What is acceptable quality delta for customers in 'dedicated' tier vs 'hosted' for INT4? Should be policy decision, table to be pushed to Product.
- For rollout, should we enable INT4 only behind model-variant flag + automatic fallback to compatible int8/fp16? (my gut: yes).

References and quick links embedded above.

Samuel: patch allocator to scoped prealloc for KV-prefetch, open PR and add unit test around stream sync (due 2028-07-31)
Claire: prepare canary checklist for enabling INT4 variant on dedicated pool (include rollback signal + eval thresholds) (due 2028-08-02)
Miguel: add IF-80 and CE-20 to nightly evals and surface per-model dashboards (due 2028-08-03)
Rina: draft product note with proposed thresholds for dedicated/hosted int4 opt-in (due 2028-08-04)
decisions: Use per-channel 2-pass clip estimation as interim mitigation for activation outliers (agreed by team)
Require IF-80 >= 90% for canary pass on INT4 variants on dedicated nodes
Rollout plan must include automatic fallback to int8 or fp16 on tail-regression detection
metrics_snapshot: Throughput: A100-40GB: FP16 120 tokens/s -> INT4 210 tokens/s (microbatch=2). Latency P50/P95: FP16 78/210 ms; INT4 45/190 ms. IF-80 pass-rate: FP16 94.8% -> INT4 90.2% (one noisy run). Hallucination probe score: FP16 0.08 -> INT4 0.13 (worse).
notes_to_self: Keep experiment names short and tag runs with kernel/CUDA/compiler metadata. When filing PRs, include perf matrix table in description. Avoid changing two variables at once (seed + batching) — observed confounding in last run.
